correctness.summary: Pendant supports are forced into every IO-code, while the remaining vertices partition into one Delta+1 set per skeleton vertex such that no two vertices in one part can both be omitted, by either total-domination or neighborhood-symmetric-difference constraints. Conversely, deleting all skeleton centers leaves matching-paired noncenters with distinct singleton traces and centers with distinct Delta-element traces. This proves gamma_IOC = n - |V(H)| exactly.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The 2026 bounded-degree IO-code paper explicitly leaves improved large-order constructions open for Delta at least 4 and suggests a density lower than the present (2Delta-2)/(2Delta-1). Searches across identifying-open-code and equivalent OLD terminology, subdivision formulations, maximum-degree constructions, and older extremal results did not locate the skeleton-lift formula. Residual risk remains from older tree literature indexed under different construction language.

value.summary: The theorem gives an exact formula for a general skeleton lift and improves the asymptotic construction benchmark for every Delta at least 4. Cycle skeletons attain density (2Delta-2)/(2Delta-1), and path skeletons give trees approaching the same value, narrowing the known asymptotic gap to the general upper bound to 1/[2Delta(2Delta-1)].

limitations: The exact asymptotic extremal constant remains unknown.
The construction does not characterize all extremal graphs or prove the known upper bound asymptotically sharp.
For Delta=3, the known 5/6 construction is stronger than the present 4/5 limiting density.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; older tree literature using different construction language remains a residual risk.
